POLICY SUBCOMMITTEE MINUTES
  MONDAY, MAY 11, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 2:00 PM

Sarah Bedy, Member  Leanna Noble, Member
Pam Chotiswatdi, Member  Patricia Scott, Member

  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Sarah Bedy called the meeting to order at 2:03 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present: Bedy, Scott, Noble

  Commissioners Absent: Lie, Killion

Also present: Jennifer Santana, Secretary.

Roll call taken by Jennifer Santana.
  • For the record, member Lie and Killion are absent and unexcused.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  26-54926  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Homeless Services Policy
  Subcommittee meeting of Monday, March 9, 2026.

  A motion was made by Voting Member Scott, seconded by Voting Member
  Noble, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  3  Noble, Scott, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Killion, Lie

2.  26-54927  Recommendation to review and discuss the City's policy on fencing around the
  Billy Jean King Library and determine whether to provide recommendations
  regarding any potential changes to the policy.

  A motion was made by Voting Member Noble, seconded by Voting Member
  Scott, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  3 Noble, Scott, Bedy

  Page 1 of 4
   POLICY SUBCOMMITTEE MINUTES
  MONDAY, MAY 11, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 2:00 PM

  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Killion, Lie

  • Chair Sarah Bedy explained that the item being discussed was a public
  comment concern voiced during the last commissioners’ meeting.
  • The subcommittee members discussed the current fencing around Billie
  Jean King Main Library. They expressed disappointment with the project and
  the lack of information or community outreach prior to the fencing being
  installed. They would like to see specific goals identified regarding how the
  project helps the unhoused population, if that is the intent behind the fencing.
  They also raised concerns about the cost of the project and stated that they
  would prefer to see those funds directed toward services for the unhoused.
  • Additional concerns raised by members included the lack of shaded areas
  for unhoused individuals in downtown Long Beach, noting that Billie Jean
  King Main Library previously provided that space. Other concerns included
  the possibility of future residential or commercial development near the
  library.
  • A member of the public provided comment and offered the subcommittee
  practical solutions, including bringing outreach, matching, and coordination
  services directly to the streets through peer support specialists at no
  additional cost to the city, with services potentially billable to Medi-Cal.

3.  26-54928  Recommendation to review and discuss the draft 2025 Homeless Services
  Advisory Committee Annual Report and policy recommendations and consider
  approval.

  A motion was made by Voting Member Scott, seconded by Voting Member
  Noble, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  3  Noble, Scott, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Killion, Lie

  • Chair Sarah Bedy mentioned that there were no new updates regarding the
  policy recommendation and annual report. No additional concerns were
  raised by the larger committee.
  • The subcommittee moved to present the draft for approval during the larger
  committee meeting in June.

4.  26-54931  Recommendation to review and discuss the proposed budget plan for the Mayor’s
  Fund pilot hygiene project and consider potential revisions.

  A motion was made by Voting Member Noble, seconded by Voting Member
  Scott, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  3  Noble, Scott, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Killion, Lie

  • The subcommittee discussed funding for the shower truck and the pilot
  portable restroom program. At this time, there are departmental funding cuts,
  and no new projects will be introduced during the current year.
  • Members discussed the pilot program funding for a portable restroom and
  hydration station, with the requested funding totaling $50,000 for a six-month
  program. Another point raised was the option of funding a pilot program that
  would utilize existing city-owned buildings while adding 24-hour security.
  • The subcommittee chair will draft a proposal to share during the HSAC
  committee meeting in June.
  • A member of the public provided comment and informed the committee that
  People Assisting the Homeless (PATH) offers grants to build capacity and
  physical infrastructure. The billing code T2033 includes laundry and hygiene
  services for the unhoused and is something that should be promoted more
  widely. Leveraging state Medi-Cal dollars could help cover hygiene and
  infrastructure costs while protecting funding from the Mayor’s Fund.

5.  26-54930  Recommendation to discuss and approve future agenda items.

  A motion was made by Voting Member Noble, seconded by Voting Member
  Scott, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  3  Noble, Scott, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Killion, Lie

  • The subcommittee will continue discussing previously agendized items,
  including the Mayor’s Fund pilot hygiene project.

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • A member of the public provided comment that CalAIM covers up to six months of rental
  arrears, which could potentially reallocate $2.1 million toward expanding shelter beds and
  addressing issues without requiring additional funding.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • No announcements.

ADJOURNMENT

Chair Sarah Bedy adjourned the meeting at 3:03 p.m.
